chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Abī Wahb, from Muḥammad ibn Manṣūr, who said:
I asked a righteous servant about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
“Say: My Lord has only forbidden the indecencies, those of them that are outward and those that are inward.”

He said: So he said, “Indeed, the Qur’an has an outward and an inward. Thus, everything that Allah has forbidden in the Qur’an is the outward, and the inward of that is the Imams of tyranny. And everything that Allah, Exalted is He, has made lawful in the Book is the outward, and the inward of that is the Imams of truth.”

key_terms.أَئِمَّةُ الْجَوْرِ: leaders of tyranny and injustice as the inward referent of what is forbidden
key_terms.أَئِمَّةُ الْحَقِّ: the Imams of truth as the inward referent of what is lawful
key_terms.الْفَوَاحِشَ: indecencies or grave immoralities forbidden by Allah
key_terms.الْكِتَابِ: the divine Book, meaning the Qur’an in this context
key_terms.بَطْنٌ: the inward, hidden meaning of the Qur’an
key_terms.ظَهْرٌ: the outward, apparent meaning of the Qur’an

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that the Qur’an has both an outward and an inward meaning?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the Qur’an possesses both an outward and an inward meaning. It interprets the forbidden inward reality as the leaders of injustice, and the lawful inward reality as the Imams of truth, highlighting a deeper Qur’anic reading connected to rightful religious authority.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Abu Wahab, from Muhammad Bin Mansour who said,
‘I asked Al-Abd Al-Salih<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) about the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[7:33] Say: But rather, My Lord has only Prohibited the immoralities, those of which are apparent as well as those that are concealed.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Quran is such that for it there is an apparent and a hidden (meaning). So the entirety of what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Prohibited in the Quran, it is the apparent, and the hidden from that are the tyrannical imams (leaders); and the entirety of what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted Permitted in the Book, it is the apparent, and the hidden from that are the Imams<sup>asws</sup> of the truth’.
en.sarwar: 10. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Wahab from Muhammad ibn Mansur who has said the following.
“I asked the virtuous servant of the Lord about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious,
“(Muhammad), tell them, “My Lord has only prohibited indecent acts committed in public or in secret,. .” [7:33]

The narrator has said that the Imam (a.s.) then said, “The Quran has an apparent essence and a hidden essence. All that Allah has made unlawful in the Quran is apparent and hidden facts in this (category) are the unjust Imams. All that Allah has made lawful in the book is apparent and the hidden facts in it (category) are the Imams of the truth (Leaders with Divine Authority).”
